story.headline: Nvidia and PreussenElektra Explore Converting Decommissioned German Nuclear Plants Into AI Data Centers
story.summary: Nvidia and PreussenElektra are studying whether decommissioned sites of German nuclear power plants can be repurposed as AI data centers. The initiative aims to cut development times by reusing existing grid connections and industrial infrastructure.

keyTakeaways: Nvidia and German utility PreussenElektra agreed on October 21, 2026, to assess former nuclear reactor sites for conversion into AI data centers.
The initiative will not use nuclear power; it aims to reuse existing high-voltage power connections, land, and cooling water infrastructure.

draft.body:
On October 21, 2026, U.S. chip designer Nvidia and German utility operator PreussenElektra GmbH announced an exploratory partnership to evaluate whether decommissioned nuclear power plant sites across Germany can be transformed into high-performance AI data centers. The initiative targets the reuse of existing heavy industrial infrastructure to shorten development timelines and reduce capital expenses during the ongoing buildout of compute facilities.

According to an official announcement from [PreussenElektra](https://www.preussenelektra.de/de/newsroom/pressemitteilungen/pressemitteilungen-2026/2026-pel-and-nvidia-explore-former-nuclear-power-plant-sites-for-ai-factories.html), the collaboration centers on assessing former plant locations for so-called AI factories. PreussenElektra, a subsidiary of the E.ON Group, manages site decommissioning, while Nvidia will supply technical criteria and operational profiles required for accelerated computing facilities.

## Reusing Grid Links Without Nuclear Energy

A central premise of the project is that it will not involve atomic energy generation. As reported by [Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/nvidia-eyes-converting-old-nuclear-plants-into-massive-ai-data-centers-reusing-shut-down-german-energy-sites-could-reduce-the-cost-and-timeline-of-building-from-scratch), the initiative focuses strictly on civil and electrical assets left behind after the reactors ceased operating.

Decommissioned stations feature existing infrastructure that modern compute facilities require, including high-capacity electricity grid connections, industrial zoning approvals, dedicated cooling water access, and available land.

[[FIG1]]

## Evaluating Eight Decommissioned Reactor Sites

Germany completed its phaseout of nuclear energy in April 2023, permanently shutting down its final commercial reactors following policy shifts triggered by the 2011 Fukushima disaster. Nationwide, roughly 30 nuclear facilities are in various stages of dismantling.

According to PreussenElektra's corporate release, PreussenElektra oversees the decommissioning and dismantling of eight of those facilities, which include sites such as Brokdorf, Grafenrheinfeld, Grohnde, Isar, Stade, Unterweser, and Würgassen. The initial review between Nvidia and PreussenElektra will evaluate conditions across these locations through a preliminary assessment to determine which properties warrant closer project design.

"Our former power plant sites have valuable industrial infrastructure and offer opportunities for new, future-oriented uses," said Guido Knott, Chairman of PreussenElektra's Management Board, in the company's release. "Together with Nvidia, we intend to conduct a sound assessment of whether and how these conditions can be leveraged for AI factories."

[[FIG2]]

## Technical Division and Project Status

The planned feasibility work splits responsibilities between the two companies. PreussenElektra will provide detailed site knowledge, regulatory framework documentation, and civil infrastructure evaluations. Nvidia will assess the requirements for AI factories and evaluate potential technical site concepts.

Markus Hacker, Senior Regional Director at Nvidia, stated in the joint announcement covered by [Mainfranken News](https://mainfranken.news/2026/10/21/preussenelektra-und-nvidia-pruefen-potenzial-ehemaliger-kernkraftwerksstandorte-fuer-ki-fabriken/) that AI facilities depend on reliable power access, ample real estate, and high-capacity infrastructure. He noted that former industrial properties can provide a viable base to develop high-performance compute capacity within Germany.

Both companies emphasize that the partnership remains at an early stage. The desktop evaluation is open-ended and designed to verify technical, regulatory, and commercial viability before any binding steps are taken. To date, neither firm has committed investment capital, finalized engineering plans, or signed construction agreements.

faq.q: Will the planned AI data centers use nuclear energy for power?
faq.a: No. The project does not involve operational nuclear power. It evaluates using the existing civil infrastructure at decommissioned plants, specifically their connections to the power grid, available land, and cooling water access.

faq.q: Which facilities are included in the feasibility assessment?
faq.a: PreussenElektra is evaluating locations among the eight German nuclear facilities it is decommissioning, which include Brokdorf, Grafenrheinfeld, Grohnde, Isar, Stade, Unterweser, and Würgassen.

faq.q: Have any data centers been approved for construction under this deal?
faq.a: No. The partnership announced on October 21, 2026, is an open-ended feasibility study. No capital investments, site selections, or building contracts have been finalized.
